profile.headline: Software Engineer at NASA/Seabrook | Aspiring Computer Engineer and Space Explorer
profile.summary: I am a first-generation student who attended the University of Houston-Clear Lake (UHCL). After completing my Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering, I plan on returning back to school to complete a Master of Science in Systems Engineering. My purpose is to become a successful engineer, work in the industry, and aid with space exploration, flight operations, and the advancement of humanity and our planet. After two years in the education field, I developed my soft skills but am finding myself to be consistently improving as a leader, active listener, and teammate as I have progressed in engineering. Additionally, engineering has allowed me to improve on my technical skills. If you had asked me two years ago about anything STEM related or dealing with the Computer Science discipline, I would have looked at you funny. Being exposed to these classes and pushing myself to be the best engineering student possible has allowed me to gain invaluable experience within these areas that will make me a valuable asset in the industry.

company.name: NASA - National Aeronautics and Space Administration

positions.title: Peer Mentor
positions.description:
The Pathways to STEM Careers is a grant-funded program that enables UH-Clear Lake to develop support services and strategies to increase student success among Hispanic and other low-income students in STEM fields.

I help to promote diversity, the importance of the STEM field, and guide those who are transitioning to the world of a university.

positions.title: Summer Intern
positions.description:
At the San Jacinto College Robotics Internship we learned skills such as coding, robot building 
and design, project management, presentation, and leadership.

Over 10 weeks, I researched, designed and  built robots, learned to code in Java, 3D print, interacted with industry users of robotics and helped to inspire students through robotics.  As a cap-stone project, I worked with elementary and junior high students on designing and programming robots with the goal of encouraging more students to pursue careers in STEM areas.

projects.title: Sequence Detector - Digital Logic Design
projects.description: Final project for Digital Circuits lab. The purpose of this project is to design a circuit that will identify a four-bit sequence using D flip flops. We were to design a state graph that described the flow of state changes to examine exactly the sequence 0101. Then, assign a binary value to each state and construct a transition table and derive the equations from the transition table. Lastly, build a working prototype using the necessary D flip flops and gates on a NI Elvis board.

projects.title: TCC Wearable Technologies hosted by the NASA Johnson Space Center
projects.description: The Technology Collaboration Center held a two day workshop on Wearable Technologies on April 29 & 30, 2019, hosted by NASA Johnson Space Center. My team and I were tasked with researching ways to improve NASA's augmented reality headsets by making changes to the design and implementing sensors that would detect sweat and chemicals secreted during virtual training.
